00742.label: Day 1 · lomustine and bevacizumab

medicines.name: Oral 5-HT3 antagonist - select ONE
medicines.dose: Ondansetron 8-16 mg total daily OR granisetron 1-2 mg total daily; prescriber selects and records agent/dose
medicines.timing: At least 30 minutes before the single Day1 lomustine dose; record delayed-emesis cover and rescue duration
medicines.note: NCCP V6 Table5 p8 and timing p4. Review QT risk, liver function, constipation and interactions. Lomustine is a single dose, not a daily course.

additional_support: Lomustine has moderate-to-high oral emetic potential. Take the prescribed prevention and rescue plan around the single dose. Contact the team if nausea or vomiting prevents fluids or essential medicines; do not automatically repeat a vomited chemotherapy dose.

Bevacizumab alone has minimal emetic potential. Routine anti-sickness drugs or steroid premedication are not automatically required for every infusion; the team may prescribe specific medicines after a previous reaction or for another reason.

Keep prescribed blood-pressure medicine and urine checks. Follow the team’s plan for any home measurements. Report wounds and upcoming surgery or dental treatment early, so timing and healing can be assessed before another infusion.

Keep steroids and seizure medicines on their own written schedules if prescribed. Ask what to do after a missed or vomited dose. Other medicines can worsen constipation; agree a bowel plan and have all new medicines checked for interactions.
Draft for clinician/pharmacist completion, not an issued prescription. Confirm agents, doses, timing, duration, interactions and rescue instructions with the current written plan.

00806.label: Day 1 · CLV, hydration and antiemetic plan

medicines.name: Individual high-risk antiemetic prevention and rescue
medicines.dose: Agent / dose / duration to be completed by the prescriber and oncology pharmacist
medicines.timing: Day 1 and delayed phase according to the agreed local regimen
medicines.note: Incomplete review row; not a prescription. Pharmacy must reconcile aprepitant/CYP3A4 and vincristine interactions; do not auto-populate a generic aprepitant bundle.

medicines.name: Cisplatin hydration and electrolyte replacement
medicines.dose: Agent / dose / duration to be completed by the prescriber and oncology pharmacist
medicines.timing: Before and after cisplatin; reassess fluid status and renal function
medicines.note: Incomplete review row; not a prescription. Complete fluids, rates, magnesium/potassium and monitoring for the actual product/local policy. No universal home fluid volume.

medicines.name: Constipation prophylaxis
medicines.dose: Agent / dose / duration to be completed by the prescriber and oncology pharmacist
medicines.timing: Start and continue on the individual vincristine bowel plan
medicines.note: Incomplete review row; not a prescription. Select laxative and escalation instructions; review bowel symptoms before each vincristine dose.

additional_support: Cisplatin has high emetic potential; lomustine adds oral moderate-to-high risk. Use the team’s prevention and rescue plan, including delayed nausea after Day 1. Aprepitant and some antifungals interact with vincristine, so the oncology pharmacist must select and check the plan; do not add medicines yourself.

Cisplatin needs fluids before and after treatment and an individual electrolyte plan. Tell the team about fluid limits, swelling, heart or kidney conditions, vomiting and reduced urine. Follow your own home-drinking advice rather than a universal volume.

NCCP recommends preventive laxatives with vincristine. Report constipation, new tingling, weakness, balance or hand-function changes before each visit. Severe abdominal pain, vomiting or inability to pass stool or wind needs urgent assessment.

Have all medicines checked, including seizure drugs, steroids, antibiotics, antifungals, non-prescription products and supplements. The team will confirm the local antifungal prevention plan and choose medicines that avoid vincristine interactions. Other infection prevention follows the individual specialist plan.
Draft for clinician/pharmacist completion, not an issued prescription. Confirm agents, doses, timing, duration, interactions and rescue instructions with the current written plan.
